Contributing to symcompR

Source: CONTRIBUTING.md

Thank you for considering a contribution to symcompR. The package ports SymPy to R, so a change is judged on two things: whether the R code is sound, and whether it gives the answer SymPy gives.

Before You Start

  • Use GitHub issues for bug reports, feature requests, documentation gaps, and questions about porting a SymPy module.
  • For larger changes, such as porting a new module, open an issue first so the design can be discussed before implementation.
  • Keep pull requests focused. A new module, a bug fix, and a refactor should usually be separate pull requests.

Reporting a Wrong Answer

A wrong result is the most valuable bug report. Please include:

  • the R input that produces it,
  • what symcompR returns,
  • what SymPy returns for the same input, if you can run it,
  • sessionInfo().

Development Setup

Install the development dependencies from the repository root:

install.packages(c("remotes", "testthat", "devtools", "roxygen2"))
remotes::install_deps(dependencies = TRUE)

symcompR has no compiled code, so no C or C++ toolchain is needed.

Porting Rules

  • Follow the SymPy source at the pinned commit recorded in inst/COPYRIGHTS. Port the algorithm, not just the output of one example.
  • Take expected values in tests from SymPy itself, run on the same input. Do not write an expected value by hand when SymPy can produce it.
  • Attaching the package must not mask any base R function. A SymPy name that clashes with base R gets a sym_ prefix, or an S3 method when base R has a generic. The test in tests/testthat/test-aliases.R enforces this.
  • Keep R code ASCII only; write other characters as \u escapes.
  • Use exact arithmetic (gmp big integers and rationals) wherever SymPy is exact. Never round through doubles in an exact code path.
  • Keep roxygen tags directly above the function they document; a helper placed between them takes over the export and the help page.

Branches and Pull Requests

  • Use one branch per logical change, named after the change (port-fu-trigsimp, fix-range-intersection).
  • Write commit subjects in the imperative (“Port the Fu trigonometric simplification routines”).
  • Keep the implementation, its tests, the roxygen source, the regenerated documentation, and the NEWS.md bullet together in the same pull request.

Code Style

  • Follow the style already used in the surrounding R files.
  • Prefer clear validation and explicit errors over silent coercion.
  • Do not add new package dependencies unless they are necessary and justified.
  • Regenerate the .Rd files with devtools::document() after changing roxygen comments.

Testing

Run the tests while developing:

devtools::test()

Before a pull request, run the full check:

R CMD build .
R CMD check --as-cran symcompR_*.tar.gz

Pull Request Checklist

Before opening a pull request, confirm:

  • Tests relevant to the change pass, with expected values from SymPy.
  • No base R function is masked.
  • Documentation is updated.
  • NEWS.md has an entry for user-facing changes.
  • No generated build artifacts, local caches, .Rcheck directories, or tarballs are committed.

Code of Conduct

All contributors are expected to follow the project Code of Conduct.
